claims.claim: Customer and government concentration are directly measurable: one customer represented 82% of Q2 2026 revenue and 40% of accounts receivable at June 30, while government customers represented 92% of Q2 revenue. This creates contract-renewal, procurement-cycle and counterparty concentration sensitivity even while government demand can validate the platform.
claims.use: Alpha risk-source input; not a numeric risk score

claims.claim: Financial-reporting controls remain an observed execution risk rather than a hypothetical one: management concluded disclosure controls were ineffective at June 30, 2026 because of material weaknesses spanning segregation of duties, accounting risk assessment, U.K. subsidiary monitoring, equity-record controls and pervasive ineffective IT general controls. Management states remediation may extend into 2027.
claims.use: Alpha governance/data-confidence risk-source input; not a numeric score

claims.claim: The same filing explicitly identifies early-stage quantum technology, possible failure to achieve broad quantum advantage, need for substantial additional capital, intense competition and reliance on government/large-enterprise sales as material risk factors. These are lawful falsifier categories for the commercialization thesis, but they are not present evidence that technical or commercial failure has occurred.

risks.risk: Q2 2026 revenue concentration was 82% in one customer and 92% in government customers, increasing sensitivity to a small number of procurement and renewal decisions.
Disclosure controls were ineffective at June 30, 2026 due to continuing material weaknesses; remediation is underway and may extend into 2027.
Broad quantum advantage, capital availability and competitive response remain explicit issuer-identified commercialization uncertainties.

contradictions.contradiction: Rapid reported commercialization growth coexists with extreme customer/government concentration and unresolved reporting-control weaknesses.
contradictions.disposition: risk clarification for Alpha; concentration and controls should be reflected in underwriting, but neither fact alone invalidates the commercialization thesis

unknowns.unknown: Whether customer concentration declines as the commercial customer base broadens in subsequent quarters.
When management testing will establish that the identified material weaknesses are fully remediated.

falsifiers: Sustained diversification away from the dominant customer and government mix would weaken the concentration-risk thesis.
Management-tested remediation of material weaknesses and effective disclosure controls would materially reduce the reporting-control risk.
Independent customer evidence of repeatable economic quantum advantage would reduce commercialization uncertainty.
